podcast.body: Released around 1978, this album is a prime example of Brian Eno's ambient music, specifically designed to be played in airports to create a calming atmosphere. "What you're hearing in the background is an excerpt from an album called Music for Airports, which was designed for, well, to be played in airports."

podcast.body: Released in 1978, this album is considered one of two masterpieces by Brian Eno that possibly marked the official beginning of minimal music. It comprised recordings made during the Berlin Trilogy period. "salían esas dos obras maestras, que dan inicio oficial a la música minimal posiblemente, que son el Music For Air por si el Music For Films."

podcast.body: This album is cited as an example of Eno's solo experiments in ambient music, moving away from traditional rock. It emphasized atmospherics, textures, and repetition, aiming for a "mode" rather than narrative lyrics. "Let's hear a bit from Eno's 1978 album Music for Airports."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This conceptual album, released in 1978, saw Brian Eno coin the term "ambient music" and create a record that, while appearing to be Muzak, was not simply intended as background music. Eno's vision for ambient music was for it to be adaptable to various levels of auditory attention, capable of being both ignorable and interesting without imposing itself. "La música ambiental debe poder adaptarse a muchos niveles de atención auditiva, sin imponer o en particular. Debe ser tan ignorable como interesante."

Composed during the same period as "Low" was being mastered and engineered in Berlin in late 1976, this album, along with "Music For Films," is considered the practical beginning of official Ambient music.

podcast.body: Portions of this "grandísima obra maestra" were recorded during the same period as the "Berlin Trilogy" when Brian Eno was collaborating with David Bowie and Iggy Pop. While primarily associated with Cologne, Eno eventually moved to Berlin, where these influential collaborations took root. "Muchas grabaciones de esa grandísima obra maestra de Brian en el Music For A Ports también es de esta época."
